check: can stale build/ state make the full GameTest run measure the wrong code
why: The run directory survives between runs, since clearRunDirectory is false, and build/libs holds a jar. If GameTest loaded that jar, a stale one could be exercised while the run appeared to test current source.
finding: It does not. gameTest/mods exists but is empty, confirmed by two independent listings including cmd dir, so no jar is placed there. Loom's gameTest run loads the mod from the project's compiled output on the classpath instead.
taskChain: gradle --dry-run shows the run's prerequisites are exactly compileJava, processResources, classes, compileClientJava, processClientResources, clientClasses, compileGametestJava, generateLog4jConfig, generateRemapClasspath, generateDLIConfig, configureLaunch, processGametestResources and gametestClasses - a self-contained chain with nothing reading build/libs.
harmlessCoexistence: build/libs does hold the remapJar at 80506fe5..., which is the release artifact. It is simply not what this run consumes, so its presence neither helps nor harms the GameTest result.
methodNote: An earlier pass reported no mods directory at all. That was the relative-path read failing silently again; the directory exists and is empty. Checking with -LiteralPath -Force and with cmd dir settled it.
